messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA reports error if SPDE-based model contains a spatial and a spatiotemporal simoutanously
parts:
Hi,
You’ll need to include a copy of your w-data with a different name, since the first argument to f() determines the name of that component.

Finn

On 11 Nov 2018, at 13:17, Neo Lyh <lyh...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi INLA group

I hope that my model contains a spatial component（S） and a spatiotemporal component （ST）, where S component is describled by a SPDE and ST component is describled by a spereable AR1 form based on the SPDE.

Here are my code,
f6stq <- y ~ -1 + Intercept+typ_appDU+typ_appST+room+bathroom+parking+storey+construction.periodC+construction.periodD+construction.periodE+construction.periodF+construction.periodG+construction.periodH+construction.periodI+dis_Bea_dir+dis_PuHigSch+dis_HealFac+dis_PuPriSch+surface+f(w, model = spde2)+f(w, model = spde2,group = w.group,control.group = list(model='ar1'))

IM6stq <- inla(f6stq,
               control.inla = list(strategy="gaussian",int.strategy = "eb",reordering = "metis"),
               family = "gaussian",
               verbose=TRUE,
               data=inla.stack.data(StackFit2stq),
               control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE,openmp.strategy="huge"),
               control.fixed= list(prec = 0),
               control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A( StackFit2stq)))

INLA reports the follwing error,
"Error in inla.interpret.formula(formula, data.same.len = data.same.len, : The covariate `w' are used in the following f()-terms: 1, 2 Only one is allowed since the naming convention of the f()-terms depends on unique names of the covariates You can resolve this as follows: Not allowed: formula = y ~ f(x, <etc>) + f(x, <etc>) + <etc> Fix: data$xx = data$x; formula = y ~ f(x, <etc>) + f(xx, <etc>) + <etc>"

How could I contains two components?
Many Thanks

--

Hi, you can’t use the same list, w.st.2q, for w2 and w. The make.index output is already a list, and you must set the names in the call to make.index, not in the inla.stack call.

Finn
